vision.purpose: The public website for **Spec4** — **reference documentation with a front page**, not a marketing site. It exists so a developer arriving from Hacker News, Reddit, or a search engine can decide in a few minutes whether Spec4 is worth installing, and, having installed it, can look up how any part works.
vision.ui_surface: Static website — hand-written HTML files, one shared CSS stylesheet, no JavaScript, no build step, served from GitHub Pages.
target_audience: Primary: Working software developers who use a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot) and read Hacker News — skeptical of marketing, allergic to AI hype, and used to judging a tool by its README and docs.
Secondary: Developers who have installed Spec4 and return to the docs via the app's Docs link.

Unified_Stylesheet.description: A single shared stylesheet implementing the site's 'look principle' — brand elements shared with the Spec4 app, reading layout otherwise — applied to all thirteen pages. Components: wordmark in the app's colors (Spec blue, 4 green, the only blue on the site); typography using the app's monospace font for code/filenames/nav version and a reading typeface for prose at proper measure and line-height; a nav of wordmark, version, and three text links with the current section marked; tables that scroll horizontally inside a wrapper on narrow viewports; code blocks as plain scrollable panels with no syntax coloring and no line numbers; figures at full column width with a caption; and a dark scheme that follows the reader's system setting via prefers-color-scheme using the app's background and text colors, with no toggle. Explicitly excludes icons, cards, hero, shadows, gradients, animation, a second accent color, and analytics.
Unified_Stylesheet.example: A reader who installs Spec4 recognizes the site's look in the tool itself.

acceptance_criteria: Every page renders without horizontal scroll of the body at 380px and 1280px viewport widths; wide tables and code blocks scroll only inside their own container.
No page loads any resource except its own HTML, the one stylesheet, the fonts, and its images.
Copy is byte-identical before and after this round: the round changes only styles.css and the minimum markup the stylesheet needs (a table wrapper, a class on the wordmark).
Text remains readable with the stylesheet disabled.
differentiators: Vs. other developer-tool sites: reads like documentation, not a landing page — the front page opens with the install command and a real artifact.
Vs. the previous version of this site: no decoration at all — the copy is the design.
Visual continuity with the app: the site's look mirrors the app's, so a reader who installs Spec4 recognizes the site in the tool.
